english.title: Keep / possess / control unregistered Schedule 4 bird
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), kept or had in your possession or under your control,

(A)_[a bird]_
(B)_[birds]_

included in Schedule 4 to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, namely **(..SPECIFY SPECIES..), which had not been registered and ringed or marked in accordance with regulations made by the Secretary of State, namely **(..SPECIFY REGULATIONS..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 7(1) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(ii) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iii) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
(iv) In relation to England, the regulations made by the Secretary of State are the Wildlife and Countryside (Registration, Ringing and Marking of Certain Captive Birds) (England) Regulations 2015.
(v) In relation to Wales, the regulations made by the Secretary of State are the Wildlife and Countryside (Registration, Ringing and Marking of Certain Captive Birds) (Wales) Regulations 2011.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one bird is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each bird (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation
